ai.title: Reorder DeepSeek V4 Flash above MiniMax M2.7 in free model picker
ai.summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash moved before MiniMax M2.7 in FREEBUFF_MODELS array and web home-client FAQ text. Mechanism: direct array element swap in constants and string literal reorder in UI component. Scope: Shared/Core constants, Web UI. Detail: Both surfaces enforce identical ordering logic manually via static data.

eli5.text: When you open the list of free models on Freebuff's website and in the app's help text, you'll now see DeepSeek V4 Flash listed right above MiniMax M2.7 instead of below it. Freebuff shuffled two entries in its internal settings and updated the frequently asked questions text to match, so the order stays consistent across the model picker and the help section. The change is live today for Freebuff users accessing the free model list or reading the FAQ.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI bumped to 0.0.88
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package version in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` is bumped from 0.0.87 to 0.0.88. This is a pure release-bump commit with no code or functional changes (+1/-1). It is part of the same-day release sequence that also reordered DeepSeek V4 Flash above MiniMax M2.7 in the free model picker, and precedes the addition of the `/live` usage dashboard and premium reset countdown.
ai.evidence: Modified file `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` shows a single-line diff bumping the `version` field from `0.0.87` to `0.0.88` in the Freebuff CLI release package manifest.

eli5.text: Freebuff's free model picker now suggests DeepSeek V4 Flash before MiniMax M2.7 when you choose which AI to use at no cost. The model list order was rearranged in both the app's settings and on the website's help page so the recommended free option shows up first. This makes it easier to pick a powerful, cost-free AI without scrolling or guessing. Upgrading means your default free model choice now points to DeepSeek V4 Flash, giving you faster and more capable assistance by default.

ai.title: Add Live Freebuff Usage Dashboard
ai.summary: New `/live` page displays real-time aggregate Freebuff usage by country and model. Server logic in `freebuff/web/src/server/live-stats.ts` queries active `freeSession` records via Drizzle, filtering expired and banned users. Client component `freebuff/web/src/app/live/live-client.tsx` renders a stylized world map with country markers and model distribution, polling `/api/live` every 15s. Footer component hides itself on `/live` route.

eli5.text: When you visit the new Live page on the Freebuff dashboard, you'll see a real-time map showing which countries are currently using the service and which models they're running, with the data refreshing every 15 seconds. The page pulls live data about active user sessions, excluding anyone whose session has expired or been banned, and displays it on a stylized world map with country markers and model breakdowns. The site footer automatically disappears on this page, and the feature is available to all Freebuff visitors starting today.

ai.title: Add Freebuff premium reset countdown
ai.summary: Added `freebuff-premium-reset.ts` utility to calculate and format the countdown to the next Freebuff premium session limit reset. The `WaitingRoomScreen` now imports this utility to display the remaining time until the quota resets, leveraging server-provided reset timestamps or falling back to timezone-based day bounds. `use-freebuff-session.ts` includes a new `refreshFreebuffLandingMetadata` function to update quota and queue depths on the landing screen when the midnight-Pacific reset occurs. Scope limited to CLI components and hooks.

eli5.text: When you're sitting in the Freebuff waiting room, you'll now see a live countdown showing exactly how long until your next batch of premium tries resets. The app watches the clock on its own and updates the timer as you wait, so you can tell whether to wait a few minutes or come back later. Once the reset time rolls around (either the server's stated time or midnight Pacific time), the waiting room automatically refreshes its information without needing you to do anything.

ai.title: Analytics sampling and telemetry env vars
ai.summary: Added `shouldTrackAnalyticsEvent` to gate high-volume events at 1% default rate. CLI and SDK now respect sampling flags and env vars `CODEBUFF_FULL_TELEMETRY` / `CODEBUFF_FULL_TELEMETRY_IDS` for debugging. Tool stream parsers replace raw contents with `summarizeToolInput` metadata to reduce payload size. Covers `common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts`, `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts`, `sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts`, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tool-stream-parser.ts`.

eli5.text: If you do anything that generates a lot of activity, like running many tools in a row or typing long messages, the app now records only about 1% of those events by default instead of logging every single one, which means your usage data is summarized and sent in a much smaller form. The CLI now respects new sampling and telemetry flags, and there are two new environment variables ("CODEBUFF_FULL_TELEMETRY" to turn off sampling for debugging, and "CODEBUFF_FULL_TELEMETRY_IDS" to target specific users) documented in the environment variables guide. This change is live today and reduces the amount of data the app sends about your actions, unless you opt in to full telemetry for troubleshooting.

ai.title: Freebuff throughput improvements via billing and logging changes
ai.summary: Added `recordMessageWithoutBilling` to `packages/billing` to bypass credit ledger writes for free-mode requests. Implemented 1% success-event sampling in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` to reduce PostHog and log forwarding load from high-volume free traffic. Updated `web/src/llm-api/helpers.ts` to invoke the new billing bypass when `isFreeModeAndAllowed` is true. Removes inline country gating checks from the completions handler, relying on upstream session validation.

eli5.text: When you use the free AI assistant, it used to pause and check country rules again on every message you sent. Now, because you already passed those checks when you first joined the queue, it skips the repeated checks and talks to your billing record more lightly, so free conversations flow faster. The change also logs and reports far less often on free traffic, which stops the system from getting overwhelmed when lots of free users chat at once. You would not see new options or text on your screen, but free responses that were coming back slowly should feel snappier, especially when many people are using the service.

ai.title: Add Freebuff auth code debug logging
ai.summary: Added detailed debug logging for invalid Freebuff CLI auth codes in `freebuff/web/src/app/onboard/page.tsx`. The logger now captures resolved auth code hash prefixes, opaque tokens, and incoming request headers (host, forwarded host/proto, origin, referer, user-agent) to aid in diagnosing auth failures.

eli5.text: The onboarding page you see when you log in to the Freebuff web app with a CLI auth code now captures more detail in its error logs when the code is invalid. If a login attempt fails, the system quietly records things like the auth code length, hash prefix, resolved token, and request headers such as host, origin, and user-agent, not for you to see directly, but so the development team can diagnose why the failure occurred. This change is live today and affects anyone attempting to onboard via an invalid Freebuff CLI auth code.

ai.title: Coerce stringified params in spawn agent tools
ai.summary: Added `coerceToObject` helper in `common/src/tools/params/utils.ts` to parse stringified JSON objects into actual objects for the `params` field. Applied via `z.preprocess` to schemas in `spawn-agent-inline.ts` and `spawn-agents.ts`. This fixes validation errors when models emit `params` as a JSON string instead of an object. Malformed strings remain untouched to ensure schema validation still rejects them.

eli5.text: When a model sends agent-launching instructions, it sometimes wraps the settings inside a quoted block (a JSON string) instead of handing them over as a ready-made set of fields. The system now recognizes that quoted block and unfolds it into the proper settings before proceeding, so launching a helper agent no longer stalls on that formatting snag. If the block is genuinely broken or unreadable, it is left alone so the built-in checks still catch and report the problem exactly as before. You would notice this the next time you ask the assistant to spin up an inside-the-app agent with extra options.

ai.title: Local token counting for DeepSeek Flash
ai.summary: Agent runtime skips remote token count API for free DeepSeek Flash agents, using local estimation instead. New helper `shouldUseLocalTokenCountForFreebuffDeepseekFlash` gates this behavior in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`. Implementation in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` replaces the `callTokenCountAPI` block for this specific model.

eli5.text: The free DeepSeek Flash assistant no longer asks a remote server to count how many words you've used before replying. Instead, it estimates that count locally on its own, which lets your request get answered faster since it skips that back-and-forth network call. This only applies if you're using that specific free assistant and you're accessing it through Codebuff. You wouldn't see this directly, but your messages would come back a little quicker.

ai.title: Cache free-mode country access
ai.summary: Added `free_mode_country_access_cache` table to store country access decisions for free-mode users. Caches `allowed` status, `country_code`, and IP privacy signals with expiration tracking. Implemented in `web/src/server/free-mode-country-access-cache.ts` and integrated into chat completions endpoint. Reduces repeated GeoIP/Cloudflare country lookups for authenticated requests.

eli5.text: When you make a free-mode request, the assistant now remembers the country-access decision instead of re-checking your IP location every time. That decision (allowed or blocked), your country code, and any IP privacy signals get saved in a new cache table that also stores when the entry was checked and when it expires. If the database is slow or down, the system still falls back to the direct country/privacy check so free-mode availability never depends on cache health. Cache writes are best-effort, so the direct result is still treated as authoritative for your current request.

ai.title: Add User-Agent header to CLI ad requests
ai.summary: CLI ad fetches in `use-gravity-ad.ts` now send a custom `User-Agent` header derived from `getCliAdRequestUserAgent()`. The web API (`_post.ts`, `impression/_post.ts`) and Carbon provider (`carbon.ts`) propagate this `requestUserAgent` to upstream services, replacing the previous browser-only assumption. This ensures ad networks correctly identify CLI traffic for targeting and billing.

eli5.text: When you run the application from the command line, it now tells advertising networks that it's a command-line tool instead of pretending to be a web browser. As a result, the ad system can correctly recognize your command-line activity for ad targeting and billing. If you looked, you would see the command-line requests carrying a custom identification header and those headers flowing through to the ad services.

ai.title: Log invalid Freebuff login auth codes
ai.summary: Added `isCliAuthCodeCandidate` to validate auth codes, triggering `logger.warn` with detailed metadata (lengths, hash prefix, params, headers) on failure in `auth-options.ts` and `login/page.tsx`. Handles array `auth_code` params. Improves debugging for malformed CLI login redirects.

eli5.text: When someone tries to log in to Freebuff using a code that doesn't look right, the system now writes down detailed information about what went wrong instead of staying quiet. Only the Freebuff team can see these notes, which helps them spot and fix problems with login links that are broken or look suspicious. You won't notice anything different when you use Freebuff, but if a login fails behind the scenes, there will now be a clear trail for the team to investigate.

ai.title: Limited DeepSeek access tier added to CLI model selector
ai.summary: Added 'limited' access tier to Freebuff model selection, introducing DeepSeek as a restricted option. Core constants updated to support tiered model filtering via getFreebuffModelsForAccessTier. CLI components (selector, waiting room, session banner) now render tier-specific quotas and labels, distinguishing 'limited sessions' from 'premium sessions'. Database migration 0052 adds accessTier field to session records.

eli5.text: When you open the Freebuff model picker in the CLI, you may now see a third quota group labeled 'limited sessions' alongside the existing premium and unlimited sections; users who previously were blocked outright because they are in a disallowed country or are using an anonymized network are instead routed to a restricted DeepSeek Flash path with a capped daily session count, and the session-ended banner and waiting room update their wording to say 'limited' or 'premium' depending on which tier your session was granted. The database now records each session's access tier so the UI can render the correct labels and quotas, effective with this release.

ai.title: Add dev-only env to force Freebuff limited mode
ai.summary: Adds FREEBUFF_DEV_FORCE_LIMITED to force 'limited' access tier on localhost. Updates packages/internal/src/env-schema.ts and web/src/server/free-mode-country.ts to bypass country checks and skip cache reads/writes when active. Scoped to dev environment via NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT check.

eli5.text: If you run the app on your own computer in development mode, you can now flip a setting (FREEBUFF_DEV_FORCE_LIMITED) to see the restricted Freebuff experience, the one where only the DeepSeek Flash model is offered, without waiting on country checks or cached data. Developers on the team working locally will notice this limited tier kicks in right away when they set that flag to true, and turning it off takes effect immediately because the system skips reading or storing cached access results for those requests. Everyone already using the live Freebuff service is unaffected; this only matters while building or testing on localhost, and only when the environment is set to dev.

ai.title: Simplify Freebuff limited-mode landing screen
ai.summary: New `LimitedLandingPanel` component replaces the generic model selector for limited-tier users, acting as a confirm gate rather than a picker. The `FreebuffModelSelector` hides the 'LIMITED' header and comparative taglines for this tier, while `WaitingRoomScreen` and `SessionEndedBanner` update session labels to 'sessions' to avoid leaking internal tier names. This change affects CLI components only, specifically `cli/src/components/limited-landing-panel.tsx` and related UI files.

eli5.text: When you're on the free limited plan and open the assistant's landing screen in the terminal app, you now see a simple confirm screen instead of a list of model options. The screen shows the single model you get, a note about data collection, your session count (e.g. '0 of 5 sessions used · resets in 8h 21m'), and a button to start a session that grays out once you've hit your daily limit. The wording also dropped the internal 'limited' label from session counters so they just say 'sessions', which reads more naturally next to the count and reset timer.

ai.title: LimitedLandingPanel button text color tweak
ai.summary: Interactable button text in `LimitedLandingPanel` now uses `theme.foreground` instead of `theme.primary`. Visual tweak for better contrast/readability. Scope limited to `cli/src/components/limited-landing-panel.tsx`.

eli5.text: You might notice that some buttons in the limited landing panel now have slightly better contrast when interacting with them. Instead of using the primary theme color, the text now uses the foreground color. This is a minor visual tweak aimed at improving readability. This change is live today for anyone using the CLI.
